stem: Why should follow-up and safety-netting in paediatric asthma remain cautious even when a child initially seems only mildly unwell?

options.text: Because paediatric asthma has the capacity to deteriorate quickly
Because chest tightness is always absent
Because spirometry is always reliable in children
Because preschool wheeze always becomes asthma
Because viral triggers can never be detected

explanation: Paediatric asthma has the capacity to deteriorate quickly. This is why follow-up advice and safety-netting should remain cautious even when a child initially appears only mildly unwell.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Children with asthma can worsen quickly; safety-netting is an important part of paediatric follow-up; mild early appearance should not create false reassurance.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because paediatric asthma can worsen rapidly, so apparently mild symptoms still require careful safety-netting.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because chest tightness may be absent or under-reported, but it is not always absent.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because spirometry is not always reliable in children and is often more difficult to perform or interpret.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because preschool wheeze does not always progress to asthma.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because viral triggers may be identified in many exacerbations and are not impossible to detect.
